claims.claim: The fixed-k problems are monotone under padding: k-Induced Disjoint Paths reduces to ℓ-Induced Disjoint Paths for every fixed ℓ≥k while preserving H3-freeness. Moreover, k=1 is linear-time solvable and every fixed-k problem is in NP.
claims.evidence: Adding ℓ−k isolated K2 components preserves H3-freeness in both directions because H3 is connected and cannot occur in a K2. Each added terminal pair is forced to use its component's sole edge, so deleting or adding these forced paths gives a bijection between solutions. For k=1, connectivity is necessary and sufficient; a shortest s–t path is induced, and BFS finds one in linear time. For fixed k, listing the at most k simple paths is polynomial-size, and all path, terminal, vertex-disjointness, chord, and inter-path adjacency conditions are polynomially checkable.
claims.witness: The padding witness consists of ℓ−k disjoint edges, with the endpoints of each edge designated as one new terminal pair.
claims.search_method: Derived the reduction and algorithms directly, then exhaustively checked all 10,650 one-pair instances on graphs through five vertices and 10,842 exact padding instances, including two-pair-to-three-pair cases.

claims.claim: Every H3-free graph is 6-degenerate, with the constant sharp; additionally, two vertices of degree at least three can never be at distance exactly three. Thus an n-vertex H3-free graph has at most 6n−21 edges for n≥7, and every connected H3-free graph of minimum degree at least three has diameter at most two.
claims.evidence: Let u-x-y-v be a geodesic of length three with deg(u),deg(v)≥3. Two neighbors of u other than x and two neighbors of v other than y all lie outside the geodesic. The two pairs are disjoint: a shared neighbor would give a u–v path of length two. These eight distinct vertices and the seven required edges form an H3 subgraph; extra edges are irrelevant for ordinary subgraph containment. Hence such u,v cannot exist. A geodesic of length at least three in a connected minimum-degree-three graph has a four-vertex subgeodesic whose endpoints contradict this fact, proving diameter at most two. If any subgraph had minimum degree at least seven, root H3 and embed its eight vertices parent-first. When embedding vertex j, its parent has at most j−2≤6 already-used neighbors but at least seven neighbors, so an unused image exists. Thus H3-free graphs are 6-degenerate. K7 is H3-free by order and has degeneracy six, proving sharpness. A 6-degeneracy ordering has at most 6(n−6)+(5+4+3+2+1)=6n−21 edges for n≥7.
claims.witness: K7 has seven vertices, 21 edges, no eight-vertex H3 subgraph, and degeneracy six; it witnesses sharpness and equality in the n=7 edge bound.
claims.search_method: Proved the geodesic and greedy tree-embedding arguments from first principles. Exact checks also covered all 13,824 seven-vertex graphs having a designated distance-three geodesic, the K7 sharpness witness, minimal H3 leaf allocations, and the edge-count identity.

claims.claim: H3-free graphs admit an arbitrary-routing-plus-matching normal form. Let R be any graph and M a matching on V(R), disjoint from E(R). Replace every edge of R by a four-edge path and retain every edge of M unsubdivided, obtaining G(R,M). Then G(R,M) is H3-free. With all terminals in V(R), induced linkages in G(R,M) correspond exactly to vertex-disjoint paths in R∪M such that every M-edge whose two endpoints are selected is itself used between consecutive vertices of one path. In particular, the H3-free class has unbounded treewidth.
claims.evidence: Every subdivision vertex has degree two, so both degree-three centers of an H3 model would have to be original vertices. A three-edge path starting from an original vertex along an R-corridor ends at its third subdivision vertex. If its first edge is in M, matching disjointness forces its next edge into an R-corridor, and after the remaining two steps it again ends at a subdivision vertex. Thus no three-edge path joins two possible centers, so G(R,M) is H3-free. Because all path endpoints are original, entering a degree-two R-corridor forces traversal of the entire corridor. Contracting traversed corridors therefore gives a simple path in R∪M, and lifting gives the inverse map. A selected subdivision vertex cannot create an extra same-path or cross-path edge without forcing selection of the whole corridor and its endpoints. Consequently, the only possible extra adjacencies are M-edges, and inducedness holds exactly when every M-edge with both endpoints selected is the consecutive edge of one path. Finally, with R=K_m and M empty, contracting the subdivided corridors yields a K_m minor, so treewidth is at least m−1 and is unbounded.
claims.witness: For every m, G(K_m,∅) is the four-subdivision of K_m; it is H3-free and contains K_m as a minor.
claims.search_method: Established the correspondence structurally and exhaustively tested 328 pairs (R,M) with |V(R)|≤4, including 3,323 exact one- and two-path-family comparisons and direct H3-subgraph searches.

claims.claim: For arbitrary graphs, hence also for H3-free graphs, k-Induced Disjoint Paths is fixed-parameter tractable in k+b, where b is the number of vertices of degree at least three. There is an exact equivalent compression with at most b+binom(b,2)+6k vertices.
claims.evidence: Let B be the degree-at-least-three vertices. Each component of G−B has maximum degree two and is a path, singleton, or cycle. A path component has attachment edges only at its ends, a singleton has at most two, and a cycle has none. A terminal-free component can occur in a solution only as a complete corridor between two distinct B vertices. Corridors with the same endpoint pair have identical external neighborhoods and at most one can be used, so one private two-edge representative per unordered B-pair suffices. Same-end, one-ended, and unattached terminal-free components cannot participate in a simple terminal path. In a terminal-bearing component, mark its terminals and its B-attachment occurrences. Any linkage either traverses every edge of a gap between consecutive marks or avoids the gap: an internal gap vertex has no other exit and is not a terminal. A one-edge gap must remain an edge, while every longer gap is exactly represented by a private two-edge path; this preserves endpoint adjacency, capacity, chords, and all cross-path conflicts. A detached cycle with one terminal is a NO instance and can be replaced by a constant-size NO instance. If q≤2k terminals lie outside B, there are q terminal vertices, at most 2q gap representatives, and at most binom(b,2) generic corridor representatives. Hence the compressed order is at most b+binom(b,2)+3q≤b+binom(b,2)+6k. Enumerating all simple path families in this parameter-bounded graph and lifting selected representatives gives an f(k+b)n^O(1) algorithm.
claims.witness: The constructive compression retains B and outside-B terminals, one private representative for each usable unordered B-pair, and one private representative for each marked gap of length greater than one.
claims.search_method: Audited every component and attachment case deductively, then compared original and compressed decisions on 95,338 exact instances: all graphs through five vertices with all one-/two-pair layouts, all six-vertex graphs with two fixed layouts, and deterministic seven-vertex stress instances. Every size bound and decision agreed.

claims.claim: A globally shortest path for one terminal pair cannot be fixed greedily, even on a seven-vertex H3-free graph.
claims.evidence: In the stated seven-vertex graph, P1=s1-y-z-t1 and P2=s2-t2 are vertex-disjoint induced paths with no edge between them. The only two-edge s1–t1 path is s1-x-t1, while the alternative displayed path has three edges, so s1-x-t1 is the unique globally shortest path. Fixing it makes a linkage impossible because x is adjacent to the required terminal s2. The graph is H3-subgraph-free because H3 has eight vertices.
claims.witness: Vertices {s1,t1,x,s2,t2,y,z}; edges {s1x,xt1,xs2,s2t2,s1y,yz,zt1}; working linkage (s1-y-z-t1, s2-t2); incompatible unique shortest path s1-x-t1.
claims.search_method: Enumerated every simple s1–t1 path, verified uniqueness and length of the shortest path, checked both proposed path families edge-by-edge, and ran an exact H3-subgraph detector.

target_evidence: The exact target asks for a complexity classification for every fixed k. The draft proves that k=1 is linear-time solvable, but neither monotonicity nor Claims 1–4 classifies any fixed k≥2 as polynomial-time solvable or NP-complete. It therefore does not resolve the requested classification at the requested strength. The surviving structural normal form, unbounded-treewidth obstruction, and branching-parameter compression are nevertheless correct and material partial progress. The final writeup expressly says that every k≥2 remains unresolved and does not claim full target coverage. Thus target_verdict is VALID_PARTIAL_PROGRESS, and the draft's claimed_resolution of PARTIAL is ACCURATE.
checks_performed: Read only the authorized source input and iteration-5 draft; used no web, retrieval database, receipt, prior run, verification report, or other solution.
